author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian list can be narrowed to one specialty on both published surfaces
summary: Both the veterinarian page and the machine-readable veterinarian list accept an optional specialty and return only the veterinarians holding it. The machine-readable list becomes a supported surface, with this filter as its first capability. Page links keep the narrowing so a filtered directory stays navigable.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> renders only veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list rather than the full one.
Every pagination link on /vets.html (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the specialty parameter, so following any link keeps the filter.
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns only veterinarians holding that specialty, in the JSON shape the endpoint returns today.
Matching is on the whole specialty name and ignores letter case; a value matching only the start of a specialty name selects no veterinarian.
A specialty held by no veterinarian returns HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON shape and an empty veterinarian list, on both surfaces.
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as an absent parameter, consistent with existing empty owner search.
Without the specialty parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave exactly as they do today, pagination included.
New behavior is covered by tests written before the production code, using real objects and no mock library, per docs/testing-principles.md.
non_goals: Any visible form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty, on either surface. Deferred to a possible follow-up request; recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md.
Free-text search for veterinarians, pets, or visits. NG-9 stays in force, narrowed 2026-08-26 by docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-free-text-search.md.
Filtering the directory by any attribute other than specialty.
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2).
Removing or reinstating REQ-VET-002, which stays withdrawn.
notes: REQ mapping: the page-surface filter and its pagination behavior sit under REQ-VET-001 (existing directory requirement); the machine-readable surface and its filter sit under REQ-VET-003, freshly minted per owner decision. REQ-VET-002 is not reused. PRD section: docs/prd.md 'Veterinarian directory'; edge cases 1-4 there are the citable list. Open questions, each recorded with the narrowest reading taken and no further product input sought: (1) a repeated specialty parameter - narrowest reading is that a single value applies and behavior beyond that is unspecified; (2) a specialty name outside the clinic's seeded list - narrowest reading is that it behaves identically to a known specialty held by no veterinarian, empty list with HTTP 200; (3) pagination of the machine-readable list - narrowest reading is that the shape is unchanged and the full filtered list is returned; (4) leading or trailing spaces around a non-blank value - narrowest reading is that they are trimmed, matching owner search; (5) the page count and item total shown on a filtered page - narrowest reading is that both describe the filtered list. Housekeeping outside my write scope: docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR, and docs/system-design.md maps VetController and VetRepository to REQ-VET-001 only.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The filter itself extends the existing paged-list pattern: an optional @RequestParam on the controller, a derived Spring Data query on the repository, pagination links carrying the parameter. That part alone would be 'minor'. Three things make this new ground. (1) The machine-readable /vets route changes status. docs/system-design.md carried it as a Known Defect ('serves no requirement, pending removal'); REQ-VET-003 makes it a published surface whose serialized shape is now a contract. That row is removed and the Contracts table rewired. (2) A caller-supplied value now reaches a repository whose sibling methods are all @Cacheable on a cache with no eviction and no size limit, on routes with no authentication. Caching the filtered query would hand any client an unbounded, attacker-chosen cache key space. New ADR records the decision not to cache it. (3) Case folding for the specialty must sit in the query, not the column: H2 and PostgreSQL store specialties.name case-sensitively, MySQL does not, so collation alone reproduces Known Defect 1 (PostgreSQL owner search) in the vet feature. Recorded as state under system-design.md Persistence. Basis for the code claims is grep plus direct reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, CacheConfiguration, the three schema.sql files, and vetList.html; the IntelliJ oracle is not connected in this run, which is the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two filtered reads alongside the existing findAll() and findAll(Pageable): a Page<Vet> form for /vets.html and a Collection<Vet> form for /vets. Neither carries @Cacheable; the two existing methods keep theirs untouched.

VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty @RequestParam; findPaginated branches on it. showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and branches the same way. Page size stays the local variable it is today.
vetList.html pagination links gain the specialty parameter. The controller must place the normalized value in the model (null when absent) for the template to read.
No new message-bundle key and no new page text. Adding user-facing wording would require all eleven locales and would trip I18nPropertiesSyncTest (REQ-LANG-002).

patterns.description: Blank-as-absent normalization precedent: null becomes empty string, then .strip(). For the vet filter the narrowest equivalent is strip-then-treat-blank-as-absent, which satisfies both the blank-value criterion and open question 4 (surrounding spaces trimmed).

Derived paged query precedent (findByLastNameStartingWith). The vet equivalent traverses the association: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable). IgnoreCase is what puts the folding in the generated query rather than the column.

Pagination link block to mirror structurally. Do NOT copy its href form. Owner links use string concatenation (@{'/owners?page=' + ${i}}) and drop the search term entirely. The vet links must use Thymeleaf's URL-parameter syntax, @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encodes the value and omits the parameter when the model attribute is null. That single form satisfies both the carry-the-parameter criterion and the no-parameter-means-today's-behavior criterion, and keeps caller text out of raw href context.
@DataJpaTest against real H2 with real seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry; six vets). This is the seam where matching semantics can actually fail.

risks.risk: theVetDirectoryShouldMatchTheSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase and theVetDirectoryShouldRejectAPartialSpecialtyName are vacuous if written in VetControllerTests. That file is a @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository, so a stub decides the result and the assertion cannot falsify the matching rule.
risks.mitigation: Place those two named tests at the repository seam (ClinicServiceTests or a new @DataJpaTest VetRepositoryTests) against real seed data. Keep the names the prd-entry specifies. The remaining nine stay in VetControllerTests, which is the right home for binding, blank-as-absent, link rendering, and JSON shape. testing-principles.md line 78 also directs new tests away from framework stubs where a real seam exists.

risks.risk: Filtered seed results never exceed five rows (surgery 2, radiology 2, dentistry 1), and the page size is five. totalPages is 1, so the pagination block never renders and theVetDirectoryShouldCarryTheSpecialtyAcrossPaginationLinks cannot observe a link against real data.
risks.mitigation: Write that one in VetControllerTests, stubbing a multi-page PageImpl. It is a rendering assertion, not a matching assertion, so the stub is legitimate there.

risks.risk: A later contributor adds @Cacheable("vets") to the filtered methods for symmetry, reopening the unbounded attacker-chosen key space on an unauthenticated route.
risks.mitigation: docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md states the asymmetry is deliberate, and the VetRepository row in system-design.md Contracts links to it.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is @ManyToMany(FetchType.EAGER). A derived query filtering on the association adds a join to both the content and the count query.
risks.mitigation: The join is a filter join, not a fetch join, so paging stays in SQL. The vet-to-specialty pair is unique in the MySQL and PostgreSQL schemas, so no vet duplicates. Assert totalPages and totalItems in the paged test to catch a count-query surprise. Note H2's vet_specialties has no UNIQUE constraint, but its seed data has no duplicate pair.

risks.risk: MySQL's default collation is case-insensitive, so a filtered query written without IgnoreCase would still pass under MySQL and fail under H2 and PostgreSQL.
risks.mitigation: H2 is the default test database and stores specialties.name case-sensitively, so the case-insensitivity test does bite in the normal suite. This is the inverse of Known Defect 1, where H2 masked a PostgreSQL failure.

notes: Verdict is 'new' rather than 'minor' chiefly because of the cache trust-boundary decision and the /vets status change; the URL-shaped behavior on its own is an ordinary extension. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: (a) new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-queries.md; (b) docs/adr/README.md index gains rows for that ADR and for the product-owned non-goal ADR 2026-08-26-non-goal-veterinarian-free-text-search.md (the first housekeeping item flagged by product-requirements-expert); (c) docs/system-design.md Contracts now maps VetController and VetRepository to REQ-VET-001 and REQ-VET-003, and Vets to REQ-VET-003 instead of em-dash (the second housekeeping item); (d) the Known Defects row 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement' is removed, since REQ-VET-003 now gives it one; (e) Persistence gains a state paragraph on query-level case folding for specialty names; (f) Open Question 5 is widened to name the caller-controlled page-number key space; (g) Threat Model gains a row for unbounded cache growth and the XSS row's vector now names the reflected filter value in URL context. No autofix audit entry: .scratch/handoff.jsonl carries no design-doc-autofix records. On the five recorded open questions I take the prd-entry's narrowest readings as-is and add no design constraint beyond them; question 4 (surrounding spaces) falls out of the OwnerController strip precedent, and question 5 (counts describe the filtered list) falls out of paging the filtered query rather than the full one. Question 3 (no paging on the machine-readable surface) means that surface uses the unpaged Collection<Vet> form.

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The whole XSS mitigation for the new reflected parameter rests on Thymeleaf behavior, and no test pins that behavior against a hostile value. I verified the mitigation independently and it holds today: the filter value only ever reaches href as a query-parameter value inside a @{...} link expression whose base is the fixed literal /vets.html (no scheme-injection seam), and the th:href attribute writer HTML-escapes the rendered value -- empirically confirmed by the existing assertion on '/vets.html?page=1&specialty=radiology', where the separator '&' comes back as '&'. So attribute breakout is impossible even before Thymeleaf's URL-encoding of the value is counted. The gap is regression control, not a live vulnerability: 'radiology' is byte-identical encoded and unencoded, so every current assertion passes unchanged if the escaping is ever lost. This slice already caught the design record asserting one false Thymeleaf fact (null-parameter omission), and the designer's own answer to that was to make a rendering assertion the load-bearing control (theVetDirectoryShouldLinkWithoutASpecialtyWhenNoneIsGiven). The second Thymeleaf assumption -- the one carrying the security weight on an unauthenticated route with no CSP -- has no equivalent control. A future contributor copying ownersList.html's string-concatenated @{'...' + ${...}} href form, or echoing the filter into text context, would ship reflected XSS with a green suite.
findings.fix: Add one rendering test in VetControllerTests alongside the existing pagination-link assertions: request /vets.html with a multi-page stubbed PageImpl and specialty="\"><script>alert(1)</script>", then assert the response body contains neither '<script>' nor an unescaped '">'. Keep it a rendering assertion over the stub, matching the placement rationale the design-block already set for theVetDirectoryShouldCarryTheSpecialtyAcrossPaginationLinks.

approved_aspects: No SQL injection seam: both new reads are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), fully parameterized, with case folding in the query rather than the collation; no string-concatenated SQL is introduced.

The caller-supplied filter value reaches no @Cacheable method. Verified by reading VetRepository: the two new methods carry only @Transactional(readOnly=true), the two pre-existing findAll methods keep their @Cacheable('vets'), and both new Javadoc blocks name the ADR. The unbounded attacker-chosen cache key space the design-block flagged is genuinely closed.

Reflected-value handling verified independently rather than taken on the design record's word: the value appears only as a query-parameter value inside @{...} link expressions over a fixed literal base path, and th:href output is HTML-escaped (confirmed by the '&' in an existing passing assertion). No th:utext, th:attr, inline JS, or event-handler attribute anywhere in the changed template.
Input normalization is total and side-effect free: null stays null, and strip-then-blank-is-null means no whitespace-only or empty value ever reaches the query. Matches the OwnerController precedent.

The /vets JSON surface does not echo the filter value into its response, so promoting it to a supported surface adds no reflection vector; the data it exposes (vet names, specialties) was already public on /vets.html, so no new data exposure.
No secrets in the diff: scanned every added production line for token/password/secret/key/credential patterns, zero hits.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the Gradle wrapper are untouched by this change set, so no new or upgraded dependency enters the tree. (Note for the record: no dependencyCheck/OWASP plugin is configured in this build, so dependencyCheckAnalyze is unavailable -- a pre-existing project condition, not a finding against this slice.)
docs/system-design.md Threat Model was updated accurately for both new rows; I checked the XSS row's mitigation text against the template as built and it now describes real behavior.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The new Persistence paragraph ends: "Owner search takes the other route and leaves case folding to the column, which is the first row of Known Defects." This is a positional cross-reference into a table ("the first row") rather than a named reference. It silently breaks if the Known Defects table is ever reordered or gains a new leading row — the same fragility the writing standards ban for "above"/"below"/"previous". Replace with a reference by the defect's own name, e.g. "...which is the PostgreSQL owner-search case-sensitivity defect (see Known Defects)." author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Round-1 autofix finding RESOLVED, and the implementer's deviation from my literal fix text is judged correct on the evidence, not on their argument. (a) My proposed 'not(containsString("\">"))' half was unworkable: grep -F on src/main/resources/templates/fragments/layout.html shows '">' closing ordinary attributes on lines 8, 9, 10, 11 and throughout, so that assertion would be permanently red against any rendered page and would be a false control, not a real one. Rejecting it was right. (b) The '<script>' half is neither vacuous nor spuriously red: the only script element in the vets rendering is layout.html:84 '<script th:src=...>', which renders as '<script src="...">' and never as the bare literal '<script>'. The assertion can only be tripped by the injected payload.

The substituted positive assertion is the stronger control and I verified it against actual rendered output rather than by reasoning: ./gradlew test --tests '*VetControllerTests*' is BUILD SUCCESSFUL with theVetDirectoryShouldRenderAHostileSpecialtyInertlyInPaginationLinks green, which is direct evidence that the rendered body literally contains 'specialty=%22%3E%3Cscript%3E' and contains neither '<script>' nor the raw payload '"><script>alert(1)</script>'. The percent-encoded string can only originate from the @{...} URL-expression encoding of the reflected filter value in an href.

The regression-detection claim holds under analysis of the two failure modes it is meant to catch. String-concatenated href (the ownersList.html form): the value would reach the attribute unencoded, the attribute writer would emit '"><script>' (so both negative assertions still pass), but 'specialty=%22%3E%3Cscript%3E' would be absent and the test fails. th:utext into text context: the raw payload appears and both negative assertions fire. So the positive assertion is precisely the control the negatives cannot be, and my stated worry (radiology being byte-identical encoded and unencoded, so nothing detects lost escaping) is closed.

Re-review of the whole diff finds no new security defect. XSS class swept exhaustively: grep -F 'specialty' over src/main/resources/templates/ returns the pagination block only; the sole other occurrence (vetList.html:20) is a th:each loop variable over vet.specialties rendered through the escaping th:text, shadowing the model attribute within its own span, and carries no caller-supplied text. No th:utext, th:attr, inline JS, or event-handler attribute anywhere in the changed template.

No SQL injection seam: both new reads remain Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), fully parameterized, case folding in the generated query. Input normalization stays total and side-effect free (null stays null; strip-then-blank-is-null), now additionally pinned by theVetDirectoryShouldTrimSurroundingSpacesFromASpecialty on both surfaces.

Cache trust boundary still closed: VetRepository.java lines 71 and 85 carry only @Transactional(readOnly=true); @Cacheable("vets") remains only on the two pre-existing unfiltered reads (lines 45, 55). No caller-supplied value reaches a cache key. Both Javadoc blocks still name the ADR.
The /vets JSON surface does not echo the filter value into its response, so the hostile-value path has no reflection vector there; the exposed data was already public on /vets.html.

No secrets in the diff: scanned every added line for token/password/secret/key/credential patterns; the only hits are prose in docs/ describing the pre-existing committed-datasource-credential condition, not new material.

Supply chain unchanged: git status reports build.gradle, settings.gradle, and the Gradle wrapper untouched by this change set, so no dependency enters or moves. No OWASP dependency-check plugin is configured in this build, so dependencyCheckAnalyze remains unavailable — a pre-existing project condition, not a finding against this slice.
